reason: The storm threatens solar power, so switching to the charged reserve directly addresses the current goal.
expectation: I expect the station to switch to emergency power, though I don't know whether that also stops the industrial loads.

alternatives.reason: The outdoor line will lose heat, so it may need attention, but the stated goal points first to the reserve.
The stored heat could help protect the garden, but I want to establish reserve power first.

effect: The reserve now powers essential loads and stops the fuel plant, but the garden's normal circulation is off, so the nook needs attention.
reaction: The dim lights and stopped circulation make the storm's impact feel immediate.
reason: The charged heat store can provide warmth in the protected nook for the garden.
expectation: I expect to place the heat store in the nook, where it can release warmth slowly; I don't yet know whether it needs another connection.

alternatives.reason: The unheated outdoor line needs attention too, but the garden has lost its normal circulation and needs protection.
The lettuce needs shelter, but placing the heat source first seems useful.

effect: The heat store is now in the nook, making it ready to shelter the crops.
reaction: The result is straightforward, though it doesn't explain how much warmth the store provides.
reason: Moving the lettuce into the buffered nook should help protect it during the storm.
expectation: I expect the lettuce trough to be placed inside the warmed nook, though it may need further care because circulation is off.

alternatives.reason: The potato trough also needs protection; I have no clear reason to prioritize it over the lettuce.
The outdoor water line needs attention, but I want to shelter the crops first.

effect: The lettuce is sheltered with its own reservoir, and its common-return couplings are capped. The potato trough still needs shelter.
reaction: Carrying the bed level and keeping the leaves clear of the screen makes the move feel practical.
reason: The potato trough also needs protection from the loss of normal heating and circulation.
expectation: I expect to move the potato trough into the buffered nook, possibly securing its separate reservoir and connections as with the lettuce.

alternatives.reason: The outdoor water line also needs attention, but I want to shelter the other crop first.

effect: Both crops are now sheltered in the buffered nook with their separate reservoirs; the outdoor water line still needs attention.
reaction: The detail of clearing the potato leaves around the screen makes the move feel practical.
reason: The outdoor line will lose its heat, and using the service tool on the trench is the only remaining combination. I don't yet know exactly what it will do.
expectation: I expect to make the exposed water line safer during the outage, perhaps by isolating or draining it.

effect: The outdoor line is drained, with its inlet closed and checks on essential power; the station is now on its planned reserve.
reaction: Draining the line is a practical response to losing its heat, and the thaw checks clarify how it can be brought back into use.

mostWorthwhile.text: Moving the lettuce was most worthwhile: capping the shared connections and carrying its separate reservoir made the garden protection feel like a practical procedure.

leastWorthwhile.text: Placing the heat store was a little thin; the result named a buffered nook but did not explain how the stored heat would serve it.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the garden's normal circulation stopped on reserve power, even though the nook had low-power outlets for survival equipment.

arbitrary.text: No action felt clearly arbitrary, although I had to guess what the service tool would do to the outdoor line until it was drained.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the station and crops fare through the storm and whether the fuel plant can resume afterward.
